graham.brief:
The Philadelphia snap counts are the strangest thing on this week's slate. Saquon Barkley played 71% of the snaps in week 1 and 16% in week 2. The books have Barkley at 16.5 rush attempts, well above the 9.5 he's averaging. The snap counts say it plainly enough.

Chicago's pass defense gives up more through the air than almost anyone, 9th-worst in the league. Chicago is the 9th-most run-first offense in football, running more than the situation calls for. So the disagreement, if there's one, lives in the player lines.

Chicago gets clean runs before contact, and Philadelphia keeps playing light in the box. Tyson Bagent is a backup who's played 14% of the snaps.

The total has slipped from 44 to 42.5 during the week. The books got to the same place by a different route. Philadelphia is favored by 3.5. Both readings come out in the middle, which is its own answer. Barkley's carry line has slipped, which usually means the books see Philadelphia throwing to catch up. The question is whether Philadelphia's plan survives contact with the scoreboard.
